message.title: Oracle to offer Snowflake as native service on its cloud
message.body:
© Reuters.

LAS VEGAS - Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) and Snowflake Inc. (NYSE:SNOW) announced today that Snowflake AI Data Cloud will be available as a native, first-party service on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, according to a press release statement.

The arrangement will allow customers to purchase and provision Snowflake directly through Oracle, with unified pricing and billing. Customers will be able to use Oracle Universal Credits to consume Snowflake on OCI.

Oracle will manage pricing, discounts, and billing for the service, providing customers with a single commercial relationship. The offering is designed to work with Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications, Oracle NetSuite, Oracle Autonomous AI Database, MySQL HeatWave, and Oracle NoSQL database.

"By making Snowflake available as a native OCI service, we’re giving customers more choice in the AI and data capabilities they can use, while simplifying how they deploy, manage, and pay for those services," said Clay Magouyrk, CEO of Oracle.

The service aims to enable data transfer through supported integrations and reduce cross-cloud data movement costs by allowing data to remain within OCI. Customers will maintain control over data access, use, and governance.

"Snowflake is excited to be the flagship AI data platform partner running as a first party offering inside Oracle Cloud Infrastructure," said Sridhar Ramaswamy, CEO of Snowflake.

The announcement was made at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas. Snowflake reported having more than 14,500 customers globally.
